description: Vertical-agnostic base taxonomy. Merged with per-vertical overlays at load time. See docs/governance/AI_GOVERNANCE_FRAMEWORK.md and policy_taxonomy_runtime_auto_fix.md.

signal_roles._description: Vertical-agnostic role -> signal subtypes. Journey/arc rules are written against roles, never literal subtypes (mirrors pillar_roles in the KPI catalogs). A subtype belongs to exactly one role. 'announcement' = the customer stating a financial intent outright; it is excluded from the behavioral (leading) composite so lead-time measurement isn't contaminated by the event it predicts. Engine intents (signal_engine.enrichment.VALID_INTENTS) are subtypes here too, so LLM-enriched signals resolve to the same roles as CSV signals. 'product_friction' = the product is disappointing the user (negative); distinct from 'usage_decline' (they use it less) and 'escalation' (they demand action).

signal_role_definitions._description: One-line, model-facing definition per signal role (what it IS / what it is NOT). Read by the signal engine's extraction prompt so free text classifies against the same vocabulary as structured sources. Every key must be a role in signal_roles.

champion_change.is: A key internal advocate or sponsor leaves, changes role, goes quiet, or is replaced.
champion_change.not: A new contact joining while the champion stays.

engagement_decline.is: The customer stops showing up: missed reviews, unanswered outreach, fewer meetings or logins.

usage_decline.is: Measured use of what they bought falls, or a KPI breaches its threshold.
usage_decline.not: A seasonal dip the customer explains.

escalation.is: The customer raises a problem above normal support: executive involvement, formal complaint, support spike.

infra_incident.is: An outage, failure, degradation or SLA breach on the delivered system or service.

capacity_pressure.is: The customer is running out of headroom they bought: power, seats, capacity, licences.
capacity_pressure.not: Asking to buy more — that is expansion_intent.

delivery_stall.is: Deployment, onboarding, expansion or time-to-value is delayed or blocked.
delivery_stall.not: A stall the customer caused and has already resolved.

commercial_pressure.is: Money or competition: competitor evaluation, budget cuts, pricing pushback, renewal risk, downsizing.
commercial_pressure.not: A decision already announced — that is announcement.

announcement.is: The customer states a decision already made: churn notice, cancellation, non-renewal.
announcement.not: Hints, threats or risks — those are commercial_pressure.

crm_flag.is: The CSM's or CRM's own risk assessment — a human judgement about the account.
crm_flag.not: Anything the customer said or did.

expansion_intent.is: The customer asks about, plans, or shows appetite for more: seats, capacity, modules, sites, refresh.
expansion_intent.not: An expansion that has already closed.

expansion_realized.is: An expansion actually closed, signed, or went live.

advocacy.is: The customer praises, references, promotes, or publicly endorses the product or team.
advocacy.not: Politeness in an otherwise negative message.

recovery.is: A previously bad metric or situation measurably improved or stabilized.
recovery.not: A promise that it will improve.

intervention.is: An action the vendor took: playbook, CSM call, credit, executive visit.

routine.is: Business as usual: scheduled reviews, ordinary tickets, feature requests without frustration.
routine.not: A request wrapped in a complaint — that is product_friction.

product_friction.is: The customer is frustrated by the product itself: bugs, complaints, usability, missing capability that hurts.
product_friction.not: An infrastructure outage — that is infra_incident.

signal_examples.text: Our exec sponsor Dana moved to a new role in ops; not sure who owns this relationship now.
Finance is reviewing all vendor spend before Q3 and asked us to justify the renewal.
Great session today — the team loved the new dashboard and asked what it would take to roll it out to two more regions.
Sending the meeting notes as promised.
